name: Palau
summary_text: Palau demands real caution. Same-sex conduct decriminalised in 2014; small, US-associated, tourism-dependent; no LGR; no documented anti-trans violence. Caveat: very small population — the evidence base is thin, so this assessment carries greater-than-usual uncertainty.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA World Database jurisdiction page for Palau: documents the legal status — same-sex conduct decriminalised in 2014.

sources.title: Human Dignity Trust
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Only the Human Dignity Trust homepage was retrievable at fetch time (no Palau-specific page); Palau decriminalised same-sex conduct in 2014.

sources.title: Over 80 Nations Support Statement at Human Rights Council on LGBT Rights - U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Geneva
sources.claim_summary: US Mission in Geneva (March 2011): post on LGBT rights in the UN context - US diplomatic advocacy for SOGI rights at the Human Rights Council; Palau was among Pacific countries supporting the call.

sources.title: Two tiny nations drop anti-gay laws: Palau and Sao Tome
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Oct 2014): Palau decriminalised homosexuality by introducing a new Penal Code with no sodomy provisions, signed by the President in April 2014 - the Attorney General confirmed the repeal; 'the benefit of legislating, rather than litigating'.

sources.title: Palau travel advice - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Foreign Travel Advice for Palau, Local Laws and Customs: official guidance for travellers including local legal customs - relevant to LGBT visitors.

sources.title: Decriminalizing homosexuality step to genuine legal equality | Scoop News
sources.claim_summary: Scoop/OHCHR opinion (Oct 2011) by Matilda Bogner: 'Decriminalizing homosexuality is an essential first step towards establishing genuine equality before the law' - notes Pacific Island countries including Palau supported the UN call for decriminalisation and equal rights.
